battle.name: 厄瓜多爾獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 瓜亞基爾河口與基多山間走廊
battle.brief: 一八二〇年五月，維卡亞總督區南部守勢已不可維持。九月八日聖馬丁於秘魯海岸登陸，十月九日瓜亞基爾駐軍幾乎兵不血刃地倒戈；十一月九日烏爾達內塔縱隊奪瓜蘭達，十一月廿二日卻在瓦奇遭阿梅里奇約五千人擊潰。火繩槍是這條戰線步槍的鼻祖，方陣的火槍隊由它起家。

kit.name: 火繩槍
kit.history: 火繩槍要點火、要瞄、要排隊。方陣把這些弱點變成了整齊的彈幕。

countries: 交戰的兩方是西班牙王國在維卡亞總督區的殘餘統治，與自一八〇九年起陸續興起的多支愛國派軍隊。皇家方面：秘魯總督何塞·德·拉·塞爾納坐鎮利馬，遙控基多；基多方面的最高軍事權力落在陸軍元帥梅爾喬·阿梅里奇手中，他自一八一六年起出任基多最高法院主席並兼皇家軍總司令，下轄秘魯王家陸軍的正規營、殖民地民兵、受雇於王室的外籍軍官，以及依附教會與大莊園主的鄉軍；兵員以混血土生人與原住民為主，軍火多由海路自利馬或布蘭卡港運入，糧秣靠穿越安第斯山口的單線驛道輸送，遠程調兵全賴騾馬運隊。愛國方面並非單一國家，而是三股力量：一是基多與安第斯高原的城市愛國派，包括一八〇九年八月十日公開會議上發難的卡洛斯·德·蒙圖法爾與主教何塞·奎羅-卡伊塞多；二是海岸派，一八二〇年十月九日瓜亞基爾響應後，駐軍副指揮格雷戈里奧·埃斯科貝多上校與詩人何塞·華金·德·奧爾梅多一系成立瓜亞基爾執政委員會，宣布自由省，並自籌經費組成「基多守護師」，由委內瑞拉籍上校路易斯·烏爾達內塔與萊昂·德·費夫雷斯-科爾德羅率領；三是大哥倫比亞的軍隊，玻利瓦爾於一八二一年二月派安東尼奧·何塞·德·蘇克雷由巴拿馬赴瓜亞基爾，而聖馬丁於一八二〇年九月在秘魯海岸登陸後，更與北方的新格拉納達戰線、科克倫的海上封鎖形成三面夾擊。愛國派的指揮系統分作兩套：一套是瓜亞基爾執政委員會，一套是守護師的軍事指揮部，兩者之間協調並不順暢；兵員、彈藥與船隻則主要靠英美商人繞過封鎖走私供給。
countriesEn: The two sides were the residual Spanish rule in the Viceroyalty of Quito and the several patriot armies that had risen against it since 1809. On the royalist side, the Viceroy of Peru, José de la Serna, sat in Lima and ruled Quito from afar; the real military power in the Audiencia belonged to Field Marshal Melchor Aymerich, who from 1816 presided over the Audiencia of Quito and at the same time commanded the royalist army. Under him served the regular battalions of the Peruvian royal army, colonial militias, foreign officers in Spanish pay, and rural levies attached to the Church and the great estates. The rank and file were mostly mestizo and indigenous; arms came by sea from Callao or the port of Huanchaco, grain along a single mule road over the Andean passes, and every long move of troops depended on pack-animal trains. The patriot side was not a single state but three currents. First, the urban criollo patriots of Quito and the Andean highlands, including Carlos de Montúfar and Bishop José Cuero y Caicedo, who raised the cry on 10 August 1809 in the open council of the cabildo. Second, the coastal current: after the revolt in Guayaquil on 9 October 1820, Colonel Gregorio Escobedo, second in command of the garrison, together with José Joaquín de Olmedo and his circle of intellectuals, set up the Junta de Gobierno, proclaimed the Free Province of Guayaquil, and raised and paid for the División Protectora de Quito under the Venezuelan colonels Luis Urdaneta and León de Febres-Cordero. Third, the armies of Gran Colombia: Bolívar sent Antonio José de Sucre to Guayaquil from Panama in February 1821, and after San Martín landed on the Peruvian coast in September 1820, the new Granada front in the north and Cochrane's naval blockade closed in on the Audiencia from three directions. The patriot command worked through two rival bodies, the Junta of Guayaquil and the military staff of the protecting division, which did not always coordinate well; men, ammunition and shipping were supplied largely by British and American merchants who ran the blockade.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩條命令線。皇家一方的總指揮是西班牙陸軍元帥梅爾喬·阿梅里奇，他自一八一六年起主持基多最高法院並兼全軍總司令，一八二〇年十一月率約五千人南下，一八二一年九月十二日在第二次瓦奇之役重創蘇克雷，一八二二年五月二十四日在皮欎查山麓兵敗投降。率領南部縱隊的老將是弗朗西斯科·岡薩雷斯上校，他於一八二〇年十一月指揮阿梅里奇的南路大軍，一八二一年八月十九日在科內被米雷斯部全殲，隨即退往基多。代表王室在南部周旋的是秘魯總督何塞·德·拉·塞爾納，他與瓜亞基爾一方的談判結果，決定王軍是撤出還是死守。愛國一方的主角是委內瑞拉籍上校路易斯·烏爾達內塔與萊昂·德·費夫雷斯-科爾德羅，兩人率「基多守護師」自瓜亞基爾北上，十一月九日奪瓜蘭達，十一月二十二日在瓦奇遭重創退回巴瓦霍約；瓜亞基爾方面則由駐軍副指揮格雷戈里奧·埃斯科貝多上校在十月九日起義中掌握軍權，並與詩人兼外交家何塞·華金·德·奧爾梅多共同組成執政委員會，其政治綱領後來寫進一八二二年的瓜亞基爾條約框架。1809年基多首義的策動者卡洛斯·德·蒙圖法爾與主教何塞·奎羅-卡伊塞多入獄後相繼病逝於拘禁中，其志由胡安·何塞·弗洛雷斯帶往委內瑞拉，一八二〇年返國再起。一八二一年二月到來的蘇克雷帶來成批火器；十月在科內取勝的何塞·米雷斯隨即在第二次瓦奇被俘，隨軍的安德烈斯·德·聖克魯斯上校於一八二一年十二月自派塔與特魯希略率一千五百人的秘魯師南下；西蒙·玻利瓦爾在北面策應，佩魯海軍的托馬斯·科克倫自一八一九年九月起封鎖卡亞俄與瓜亞基爾，扼住王軍的彈藥命脈。愛國派游擊隊指揮官加夫列爾·加西亞·戈麥斯是西班牙籍出身，一八二一年一月四日塔尼薩瓜之役被俘後遭槍決，頭顱被送回基多示眾。
peopleEn: The decisive figures belong to two separate chains of command. On the royalist side the overall commander was the Spanish field marshal Melchor Aymerich, who presided over the Audiencia of Quito from 1816 while also holding supreme command of the royalist army. He marched south with around 5,000 men in November 1820, mauled Sucre at the Second Battle of Huachi on 12 September 1821, and was defeated and compelled to surrender on the slopes of Pichincha on 24 May 1822. The veteran who led the southern column was Colonel Francisco González, who commanded Aymerich's main force southward in November 1820 and was annihilated by Mires's troops at Cone on 19 August 1821, after which he withdrew towards Quito. The royal authority that maneuvered over the south was the Viceroy of Peru, José de la Serna: the terms he accepted in negotiation with Guayaquil decided whether the royal troops would leave or stand fast. On the patriot side the leading figures were the Venezuelan colonels Luis Urdaneta and León de Febres-Cordero, who led the División Protectora de Quito north from Guayaquil, took Guaranda on 9 November and were badly hit at Huachi on 22 November, falling back to Babahoyo. At Guayaquil the military power of the rising was held by Colonel Gregorio Escobedo, second in command of the garrison, who acted with the poet and diplomat José Joaquín de Olmedo to form the Junta de Gobierno; the political line they set out later framed the Treaty of Guayaquil of 1822. The men who had raised the cry of 1809, Carlos de Montúfar and Bishop José Cuero y Caicedo, died in confinement; their cause was carried to Venezuela by Juan José Flores, who returned to Ecuador in 1820. Sucre arrived in February 1821 with large deliveries of weapons; José Mires, who won at Cone in August, was taken prisoner at the Second Battle of Huachi in September; Colonel Andrés de Santa Cruz sailed south with a Peruvian division of 1,500 men from Paita and Trujillo in December 1821. Simón Bolívar worked the northern front while Thomas Cochrane, commanding at sea for Peru, had blockaded Callao and Guayaquil since September 1819, strangling the royalists' supply of powder and shot. The patriot guerrilla commander Gabriel García Gómez, a Spaniard by birth, was captured at Tanizagua on 4 January 1821, shot, and his head sent back to Quito for display.
kits: 本卡兵器火繩槍是這條戰線步槍的鼻祖。一五二〇年前後的西班牙火繩槍為滑膛，槍管鑄接或捲焊，槍托連成可抵在胸前的支架，槍機靠一條燃燒的火繩扳動擊錘；射手要先點火、把火繩搭在扳機上、舉槍瞄準，依程序分層放列，射完退入矛兵掩體內裝填。這種武器有三重弱點：射速慢、怕雨怕夜、每名射手都要隨身攜帶火繩盤與支架。它的真正價值在於確定了三條沿用至今的規矩。一是以長矛隊與火槍隊混編的方陣為骨架，火槍隊按層次輪替射擊，射擊的時機由口令統一掌握，射線之內不留空檔。二是密集線列與齊射紀律，使零散的火門變成一片可以覆蓋正面遠距離的彈幕，方陣的弱點因此被秩序抵銷。三是火繩槍的槍托支架使火槍隊在必要時仍能手持一支帶刺的短槍近身格鬥，後來刺刀接上槍口，長矛與火槍合流為刺槍並用的步兵。一八二〇年的線上，技術血緣已走到燧發滑膛步槍：槍機由火繩改為擊錘打燧石，原理相同但不再依賴火繩，射速與全天候作戰能力大為提升，而「線列、齊射、層次輪替」的戰術則原封不動地承襲下來。蘇克雷於一八二一年二月自巴拿馬運到的軍火清單最能說明這一點：一千支步槍、五萬發步槍彈、八千塊燧石、五百把馬刀、一百對手槍，全部是燧發系統，說明一八二〇年皇家軍與愛國軍都早已不用火繩槍；火繩槍在這場戰爭的位置，是整個西班牙步槍譜系的源頭，而不是戰場上的實配。其餘裝備方面，皇家軍有秘魯鑄造的中小口徑野戰炮與基多城防重炮，愛國軍在瓜亞基爾有河用小炮與武裝快艇；皇家軍靠數百匹馬與騾子組成的運隊翻越山口，愛國軍則靠瓜亞基爾河汊的平底船、馬背馱運與沿海走私帆船，維持瓜蘭達、巴瓦霍約與安巴托一線的補給。科克倫的封鎖艦隊也迫使兩方都尋求搶船奪船的快速手段。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card, the matchlock musket, is the ancestor of the muskets that fought along this front. The Spanish matchlock of around 1520 was a smoothbore with a cast or wound barrel whose stock formed a rest for the breast; the lock was worked by a burning cord that pulled the hammer, so a soldier had to light the match, lay it on the lock, bring the musket to his shoulder and fire in a prescribed order, the ranks rotating back behind the pikes to reload. It had three weaknesses: slow rate of fire, useless in rain and at night, and the burden of carrying a match and a rest for every man. Its real significance lay in fixing three rules that lasted for centuries. First, the pike-and-shot formation: musketeers fired by ranks in rotation under a single command, so that no interval opened inside the firing line. Second, close line and disciplined volley fire, which turned scattered shots into a curtain covering the front at long range, and let the order of the formation neutralize the weakness of the weapon. Third, the rest built into the stock allowed a musketeer to fight at close quarters with the same piece, and the bayonet later fixed to the muzzle united pike and shot into a single infantry arm. By 1820 the technical line had reached the flintlock smoothbore musket: the cord gave way to the hammer striking a flint, the principle unchanged but the match no longer required, with a much better rate of fire and all-weather capability, while the tactics of line, volley and rank rotation passed down unchanged. The most telling evidence is the shipment Sucre brought from Panama in February 1821: 1,000 muskets, 50,000 musket rounds, 8,000 flints, 500 sabers and 100 pairs of pistols, every item a flintlock system, which shows that neither the royalist nor the patriot army of 1820 still used the matchlock. The matchlock's place in this war is therefore as the fountainhead of the whole Spanish musket lineage, not as an issue of the battlefield. As for the rest of the equipment, the royalists had small-bore field guns cast in Peru and heavy guns for the defenses of Quito, while the patriots at Guayaquil had river guns and armed boats; the royal army moved its columns over the passes on trains of several hundred horses and mules, and the patriots kept the line through Guaranda, Babahoyo and Ambato alive with flat-bottomed boats on the Guayas channels, packhorses and coastal smuggling schooners. Cochrane's blockading squadron also forced both sides to seize and retake ships by fast cutting-out expeditions.
tactics: 一八二〇年十一月九日的卡米諾雷亞爾山口一役，是這場戰爭戰術的縮影。愛國派在瓜亞基爾通往瓜蘭達的驛道上一條戰略山徑設伏，皇家縱隊因地形被迫拉成單列，愛國派集中封鎖谷口，靠近距離的齊射與火槍隊的輪替射擊守住隘路，隨即奪取瓜蘭達。皇家派在瓦奇一役採用的則是縱隊正面進攻：阿梅里奇以約五千人自瓜蘭達沿山路南推，先頭部隊試探之後，密集步兵縱隊在起伏地形上展開正面衝鋒，炮兵在側翼支援，騎兵壓制兩翼。其結果是愛國派以約二千人對五千人，縱隊被地形拉長、火力無法同時展開，慘敗。愛國派在巴瓦霍約的抵抗體現另一種打法：把殘兵與補充兵合共約三百人、其中騎兵約五十，組成縱隊，依托河汊與碼頭作最後據守，並派游擊隊深入高地襲擾，試圖以機動換取時間；結果是一八二一年一月四日塔尼薩瓜的游擊隊在山中被殲滅，指揮官加夫列爾·加西亞·戈麥斯被俘後遭槍決並梟首示眾，瓜亞基爾執政委員會第一次軍事嘗試就此告吹。蘇克雷到任後把戰術拉回正面：他企圖以兩翼鉗形同時壓迫基多，命米雷斯率偏師迎擊岡薩雷斯縱隊，八月十九日在科內將其全殲，九月二日主力進駐瓜蘭達；但九月十二日第二次瓦奇，他仍照舊以步兵正面對攻，又一次被阿梅里奇擊潰，陣亡八百人、被俘五十人，其中就有米雷斯本人，只好在十一月十九日於巴瓦霍約簽下九十日停戰。一八二二年冬，他改採兩面夾攻：北方由玻利瓦爾在帕斯托方向牽制，南方由聖馬丁派出的秘魯師自派塔與特魯希略下來，一千五百人，含三個騎兵中隊與一個炮兵團；一八二二年一月新攻勢開始，五月二十四日於皮欎查山麓一役，蘇克雷以散兵線加熟悉山路的嚮導奪取陣地，皇家軍主力崩潰。總的來說，一八二〇年這條戰線的勝負關鍵，是誰能控制瓜亞基爾河口的海運與山口的馳援：掌握海運者得彈藥，掌握山口者得主動。
tacticsEn: The action at the Camino Real pass on 9 November 1820 is the tactical miniature of the whole war. The patriots ambushed a strategic mountain track on the road from Guayaquil to Guaranda; the royalist column was forced by the ground into a single file, the patriots sealed the defile with concentrated close-range volleys and with musketeer ranks firing in rotation, and Guaranda was taken immediately afterwards. At Huachi the royalists fought the other way, with a column attack: Aymerich pushed some 5,000 men south from Guaranda along the mountain road, and after the leading troops reconnoitred, dense infantry columns went forward in frontal assault on broken ground, with artillery on the flanks and cavalry covering the wings. The result was that 2,000 patriots faced 5,000 royalists, the column was stretched by the terrain, the fire could not be brought to bear simultaneously, and the patriots were crushed. The stand at Babahoyo illustrates a different method: survivors and reinforcements, about 300 men in all with some 50 cavalry, were formed into a detachment holding the river channels and the landing stage as a last redoubt, while guerrilla bands pushed into the highlands to harass the enemy and trade mobility for time. The gamble failed when the guerrillas were destroyed in the mountains at Tanizagua on 4 January 1821, and their commander Gabriel García Gómez, taken prisoner, was shot and beheaded, his head carried back to Quito; the first military attempt of the Junta of Guayaquil ended there. On his arrival Sucre pulled tactics back to the frontal: he planned a pincer on Quito, sent General Mires with a detached force against González's column, annihilated it at Cone on 19 August, and occupied Guaranda with his main body on 2 September. Yet on 12 September, at the Second Battle of Huachi, he again offered a frontal infantry attack and was beaten a second time by Aymerich, losing 800 men killed and 50 prisoners, Mires among them, and he had to sign a ninety-day truce at Babahoyo on 19 November. In the winter of 1822 he changed to a two-sided offensive: Bolívar distracted the north in the Pasto direction while San Martín sent a Peruvian division of 1,500 men down from Paita and Trujillo, with three cavalry squadrons and one artillery regiment. The new offensive opened in January 1822, and on 24 May, on the slopes of Pichincha, Sucre took his positions with skirmish lines and local guides and the royalist main body collapsed. In the end, the question on this front in 1820 was who controlled the shipping of the Guayaquil estuary and who controlled reinforcement of the passes: control of the sea brought ammunition, control of the passes brought initiative.
data: 可核對的數字集中在1820年下半年到1822年5月。基多城在1809年人口約一萬；1819年8月7日波亞卡戰役標誌新格拉納達解放；1820年9月8日聖馬丁率解放軍於秘魯海岸登陸，同月科克倫的封鎖仍在進行。10月9日瓜亞基爾起義幾乎兵不血刃，10月18日波多維耶霍、11月3日昆卡相繼響應，獨立浪潮由河口推向內陸。守護師方面：11月7日完成向安第斯山區的推進部署，11月9日卡米諾雷亞爾山口得手，11月11日拉塔昆加與里奧班巴、11月12日安巴托宣布獨立；阿梅里奇隨即以約五千人南下，愛國派在安巴托一線僅約二千人，11月22日瓦奇一役潰敗，殘部退到巴瓦霍約，重新組織的守軍總數約三百人，其中騎兵約五十；1821年1月4日塔尼薩瓜游擊隊覆滅。1821年2月蘇克雷抵瓜亞基爾，隨船軍火為1,000支步槍、50,000發步槍彈、8,000塊燧石、500把馬刀、100對手槍；8月19日科內之役全殲岡薩雷斯縱隊，9月2日主力佔領瓜蘭達，9月12日第二次瓦奇愛國派陣亡約八百人、被俘五十人，11月19日簽九十日停戰；1821年12月自派塔與特魯希略南下的秘魯師為1,500人，含三個騎兵中隊與一個炮兵團；1822年5月24日皮欎查之役皇家軍投降，5月25日蘇克雷入基多，接受維卡亞總督區全部西班牙軍隊的投降。關於1820年五月這個時點本身的具體戰鬥，史料記載有限，諸說並存：有的說法視五月為皇家軍收縮南部、愛國方整軍再舉的節點，有的把轉折點放在九月聖馬丁登陸之後的連鎖效應；較保守的處理，是只把五月當作這條戰線轉入攻勢的起點。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are concentrated between the second half of 1820 and May 1822. Quito had a population of about ten thousand in 1809. The Battle of Boyacá on 7 August 1819 marked the liberation of New Granada, and on 8 September 1820 San Martín landed his Liberating Expedition on the Peruvian coast while Cochrane's blockade was still in force. The revolt in Guayaquil on 9 October was almost bloodless; Portoviejo followed on 18 October and Cuenca on 3 November, so the wave of independence ran from the estuary into the interior. On the patriot side: the División Protectora de Quito was in position to enter the Andes by 7 November, won the pass at Camino Real on 9 November, and saw Latacunga and Riobamba proclaim independence on 11 November and Ambato on 12 November. Aymerich replied by sending about 5,000 men south, against a patriot force of some 2,000 in the Ambato area; the defeat at Huachi on 22 November threw the survivors back onto the coastal plain at Babahoyo, where the re-formed garrison numbered about 300 men including some 50 cavalry, and on 4 January 1821 the Tanizagua guerrillas were wiped out. Sucre reached Guayaquil in February 1821 with 1,000 muskets, 50,000 musket rounds, 8,000 flints, 500 sabers and 100 pairs of pistols. His column annihilated González's force at Cone on 19 August, occupied Guaranda on 2 September, lost about 800 men killed and 50 prisoners at the Second Battle of Huachi on 12 September, and signed a ninety-day truce on 19 November. The Peruvian division that sailed down from Paita and Trujillo in December 1821 numbered 1,500 men with three cavalry squadrons and one artillery regiment. At Pichincha on 24 May 1822 the royalist army capitulated, and on 25 May Sucre entered Quito and accepted the surrender of every Spanish force in the Audiencia. As for May 1820 itself, the record is thin and the accounts differ: some readings treat the month as the point at which the royal army contracted in the south and the patriots reorganized, others place the turning point in the chain reaction that followed San Martín's landing in September. The conservative treatment is to take May simply as the moment this front turned from defence to attack.
cause: 一場戰爭的起因往往是幾層壓力同時收緊。第一層是身分與地位的僵局：十八世紀末的基多是南美洲的教育與宗教中心之一，城內住著一批受過良好教育的克里奧爾商人、律師、教士與軍官，而總督區的官職、主教席位與軍銜幾乎全部讓給從西班牙本土出生的斯潘尼亞爾，本地精英在政治與經濟上都沒有出口，徵稅、徵兵與鎮壓年年加劇。第二層是啟蒙與拿破崙戰爭的衝擊：法國革命與歐洲戰事令西班牙波旁王朝的合法性受到普遍懷疑，克里奧爾知識分子引用孟德斯鳩與盧梭的語彙，「效忠人民而非效忠君王」的敘事在1810年後的西班牙美洲各地同時出現。第三層是外部示範：委內瑞拉1809年至1823年、墨西哥1810年至1821年的起義，玻利瓦爾1819年8月7日波亞卡戰役的勝利，都證明西班牙正統可以被擊敗；而1818年拉巴達河口一役之後英國的海上封鎖，又切斷了王室從歐洲補充兵員與軍火的渠道。第四層是經濟上的轉向：科克倫自1819年9月起封鎖卡亞俄與瓜亞基爾，港口城市的航運生意被壓縮，軍火與私貨的走反而讓瓜亞基爾的商界與軍官與愛國派建立了聯繫。第五層是直接導火線：1809年8月10日基多的公開會議上，主教何塞·奎羅-卡伊塞多與卡洛斯·德·蒙圖法爾提出的自治方案遭總督府迴避，遂引發當日的軍事起事與對總督府的對峙。雖然兩個月後起事被平定，此後十年總督區每一次加稅、每一次抓捕、每一次鎮壓，都在為1820年南部的反攻儲備人馬；而1809年至1812年間的戰敗、1812年伊瓦拉一役的鎮壓與此後長達七年的皇家控制，則把這場起事壓回地底，直到1820年才重新爆開。
causeEn: The origins of such a war usually lie in several pressures tightening at once. The first was a deadlock of status and rank: by the end of the eighteenth century Quito was one of the educational and religious centres of South America, home to a well-educated body of criollo merchants, lawyers, clerics and army officers, yet the offices, bishoprics and commissions of the Audiencia were reserved almost entirely for Spaniards born in the mother country, so the local elite had no outlet in politics or in trade, while taxation, recruitment and repression grew year by year. The second was the shock of the Enlightenment and of the Napoleonic wars: the French Revolution and the European fighting made the legitimacy of the Spanish Bourbon dynasty a subject of general doubt, and criollo intellectuals began to use the language of Montesquieu and Rousseau, so that the claim of loyalty to the people rather than to the king appeared in Spanish America simultaneously after 1810. The third was demonstration from outside: the revolts in Venezuela from 1809 to 1823 and in Mexico from 1810 to 1821, and above all Bolívar's victory at Boyacá on 7 August 1819, proved that the Spanish crown could be beaten, while the British blockade after the battle of the River Plate in 1818 cut the crown off from Europe for men and munitions. The fourth was an economic turn: Cochrane's blockade of Callao and Guayaquil from September 1819 squeezed the carrying trade of the port cities and drove the smuggling of arms and contraband into exactly the channels that tied Guayaquil's merchants and officers to the patriots. The fifth was the immediate spark. At the open council of Quito on 10 August 1809, the autonomy proposals of Bishop José Cuero y Caicedo and Carlos de Montúfar were sidestepped by the viceregal government, and the result was a military rising that day and a confrontation with the authorities. It was put down within two months, but for the next ten years every new tax, every arrest and every repression in the Audiencia was storing up men for the counter-stroke from the south in 1820, while the defeats of 1809 to 1812, the repression after the Battle of Ibarra of 1812 and seven further years of firm royal control kept the rising underground until it broke open again in 1820.
impact: 其一，1820年這條南部戰線是西屬美洲革命能夠連成一條線的技術前提：只有當瓜亞基爾的港口、巴瓦霍約的船隊與安第斯山口的驛道可以被愛國派用來運兵運槍，北面的玻利瓦爾與南面的聖馬丁才可能在1822年同時壓向基多，維卡亞總督區才會在兩年內解體；反過來說，沒有1820年的南部建制，1822年的皮欎查就只是又一次孤軍深入的冒險。其二，這條戰線的慘敗也改造了愛國派的戰爭方法：1820年11月瓦奇的敗績說明，靠臨時編成的民兵與零散游擊無法對抗有紀律、有後勤的縱隊；此後蘇克雷堅持以正規營制、統一火藥供應與兩翼鉗形作戰，才在皮欎查取勝；1821年2月那一船火器之所以重要，正是因為它把軍隊從民兵體質改造成可用炮兵與騎兵支援的正規軍。其三，維卡亞總督區解體後，邊界問題立刻成為國際問題：1822年7月的瓜亞基爾會議上，玻利瓦爾力主成立以大哥倫比亞為核心的南美共和國，聖馬丁代表秘魯政府反對，會議不果而散；1822年9月27日簽訂的瓜亞基爾條約劃定了秘魯與大哥倫比亞的邊界，把北部爭端推給日後的談判，後來一八四〇年代的一條河糾紛與一八八〇年代的地質爭議都由此發端。其四，這場戰爭為大哥倫比亞的解體埋下伏線：1824年秘魯反對玻利瓦爾的集權，1826年玻利瓦爾進軍波托西，聯邦旋即分裂，厄瓜多爾、委內瑞拉與新格拉納達分立，1820年這一戰的果實，最終落進了三個共和國的邊界線上。其五，獨立並未帶來秩序：皇家派殘部在帕斯托一帶抵抗，1822年4月7日邦博納與4月20日埃爾佩尼爾兩役之後玻利瓦爾才進軍帕斯托，同年12月帕斯托地區的武裝反攻與其後殘酷鎮壓，1824年第二次伊瓦拉戰役與阿瓜隆戈於1824年7月13日被處決，都說明這條安第斯山脈上的邊界線，仍要用槍桿與砲口反覆丈量。
impactEn: First, the southern front of 1820 was the technical precondition for the Spanish American revolutions to become a single connected war: only when the port of Guayaquil, the boats of Babahoyo and the mule roads over the Andean passes could be used by the patriots to move men and muskets could Bolívar in the north and San Martín in the south press on Quito at the same time in 1822 and dissolve the Audiencia in the space of two years; conversely, without the southern organization built in 1820, Pichincha in 1822 would have been one more raid by a lone army. Second, the disasters on this front also reshaped how the patriots fought: the defeat at Huachi in November 1820 showed that improvised militia and scattered guerrillas could not stand against a disciplined column with supply, and after it Sucre insisted on regular battalion organization, centralized powder supply and the pincer movement, which is how he won at Pichincha; the shipment of arms in February 1821 mattered precisely because it turned a militia into an army that artillery and cavalry could support. Third, once the Audiencia had been dissolved the question of frontiers became international at once. At the conference of Guayaquil in July 1822 Bolívar pressed for a South American republic centred on Gran Colombia and San Martín spoke for the Peruvian government against it, and the conference broke up without result; the Treaty of Guayaquil of 27 September 1822 then fixed the border between Peru and Gran Colombia and pushed the northern dispute into later negotiations, from which the 1840s Rio de la Plata boundary quarrel and the 1880s geological dispute both grew. Fourth, the war laid the groundwork for the dissolution of Gran Colombia: Peru opposed Bolívar's centralization in 1824, Bolívar marched into Potosí in 1826, the federation broke apart and Ecuador, Venezuela and New Granada went their separate ways, so that the fruit of the fighting of 1820 ended up drawn on the border lines of three republics. Fifth, independence brought no order. Royalist remnants held out around Pasto, and only after Bomboná on 7 April 1822 and El Peñol on 20 April did Bolívar enter Pasto; the armed rising in that district in December 1822 and the harsh reprisals that followed, the Second Battle of Ibarra in 1824 and the execution of Agualongo on 13 July 1824 all show that the line drawn along the Andes was still being measured with rifle and cannon long after the war was over.
result: 1820年這條戰線的直接結果是失敗的。愛國派在瓜亞基爾建立的「自由省」軍事機構在安巴托與瓜蘭達方向被阿梅里奇以兩倍兵力的縱隊擊穿，1820年11月22日瓦奇之役之後殘部退保巴瓦霍約，1821年1月4日塔尼薩瓜的游擊隊覆滅，執政委員會第一次北上企圖完全破滅，1821年11月19日更在巴瓦霍約簽下九十日停戰，等於承認皇家派仍控制基多與中部高地。但同樣是1820年，局勢的根本轉折也已經完成：瓜亞基爾等河口城市脫離王權，瓜亞基爾的政權機構與民間武裝在失敗中鍛造成軍，蘇克雷自巴拿馬運來的成批火器在同一年被引進南方，聖馬丁的登陸又抽走了秘魯總督區可用於南線的兵力。結果是1821年的戰局在北面與南面同時逆轉：蘇克雷的偏師於8月19日在科內消滅岡薩雷斯的縱隊，12月的秘魯師自派塔與特魯希略南下，1822年1月新一輪攻勢開始，5月24日皮欎查山麓一役皇家軍主力被殲，5月25日蘇克雷進入基多，接受維卡亞總督區全部西班牙軍隊的投降，統治三百年的西班牙王權在厄瓜多爾本土就此終結。
resultEn: The immediate outcome of this front in 1820 was failure. The military machinery of the Free Province of Guayaquil was broken through in the Ambato and Guaranda direction by Aymerich's column, twice as numerous as the patriot force; after the defeat at Huachi on 22 November 1820 the survivors fell back to defend Babahoyo, the guerrillas were destroyed at Tanizagua on 4 January 1821, the first northern offensive of the Junta of Guayaquil was completely ruined, and the ninety-day truce signed at Babahoyo on 19 November 1821 amounted to an acknowledgement that the royalists still held Quito and the central highlands. But in that same year of 1820 the decisive turn of the whole situation had already been made: the river-mouth cities including Guayaquil had broken with royal authority, the government and the armed bands of Guayaquil had been forged in defeat, the bulk shipment of arms brought by Sucre from Panama had been carried into the south in the same year, and San Martín's landing had drawn off the forces the viceroy of Peru could still find for the southern front. As a result the war turned in the north and the south at once during 1821: Sucre's detached force destroyed González's column at Cone on 19 August, the Peruvian division came down from Paita and Trujillo in December, the new offensive opened in January 1822, the royalist main body was destroyed on the slopes of Pichincha on 24 May, and on 25 May Sucre entered Quito and accepted the surrender of every Spanish force in the Audiencia. Three centuries of Spanish royal rule on Ecuadorian soil came to an end.
